en: Itivuttaka 104: Catukkanipāta, Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of gifts. What four? The gift of material things, the gift of Dhamma, the gift of safety, and the gift of loving-kindness. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of gifts. When this was said, a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, what is the difference between one who gives a gift of material things and one who gives a gift of Dhamma?

“Brahmin, the giver of a gift of material things gives for the sake of some benefit in this very life, or for the sake of fame, or out of fear, or because he expects something in return; but the giver of a gift of Dhamma gives for the sake of his own purification, for the sake of the purification of others, or out of compassion for the world, thinking: ‘May this lead to the welfare and happiness of many people. This, brahmin, is the difference between one who gives a gift of material things and one who gives a gift of Dhamma. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The person who is intent on his own welfare but not on the welfare of others; the person who is intent on the welfare of others but not on his own welfare; the person who is intent neither on his own welfare nor on the welfare of others; and the person who is intent both on his own welfare and on the welfare of others. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of offerings. What four? The offering made by one who is not self-controlled to one who is not self-controlled; the offering made by one who is not self-controlled to one who is self-controlled; the offering made by one who is self-controlled to one who is not self-controlled; and the offering made by one who is self-controlled to one who is self-controlled. Of these four kinds of offerings, bhikkhus, the offering made by one who is self-controlled to one who is self-controlled is the most fruitful and productive of great fruit. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a heap of filth; the individual who is like a lotus pond; the individual who is like a jewel casket; and the individual who is like a great ocean. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a shallow pool; the individual who is like a deep pool; the individual who is like a clear pool; and the individual who is like a turbid pool. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small stream; the individual who is like a large river; the individual who is like a rain cloud; and the individual who is like a great cloud. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small fire; the individual who is like a large fire; the individual who is like a lightning flash; and the individual who is like a great thundercloud. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small tree; the individual who is like a large tree; the individual who is like a flowering tree; and the individual who is like a fruit-bearing tree. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small mountain; the individual who is like a large mountain; the individual who is like a golden mountain; and the individual who is like a mountain of jewels. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small forest; the individual who is like a large forest; the individual who is like a flowering forest; and the individual who is like a fruit-bearing forest. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small grove; the individual who is like a large grove; the individual who is like a flowering grove; and the individual who is like a fruit-bearing grove. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small lake; the individual who is like a large lake; the individual who is like a clear lake; and the individual who is like a turbid lake. The individual who is like a small pond; the individual who is like a large pond; the individual who is like a clear pond; and the individual who is like a turbid pond. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small river; the individual who is like a large river; the individual who is like a clear river; and the individual who is like a turbid river. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small ocean; the individual who is like a large ocean; the individual who is like a clear ocean; and the individual who is like a turbid ocean. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small cloud; the individual who is like a large cloud; the individual who is like a clear cloud; and the individual who is like a turbid cloud. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small rain cloud; the individual who is like a large rain cloud; the individual who is like a clear rain cloud; and the individual who is like a turbid rain cloud. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small mountain peak; the individual who is like a large mountain peak; the individual who is like a clear mountain peak; and the individual who is like a turbid mountain peak.

These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small mountain cave; the individual who is like a large mountain cave; the individual who is like a clear mountain cave; and the individual who is like a turbid mountain cave. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The individual who is like a small mountain pass; the individual who is like a large mountain pass; the individual who is like a clear mountain pass; and the individual who is like a turbid mountain pass. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of individuals. [The Blessed One then spoke further: “There are these four kinds of individuals. What four? The Discourse on Being Perfect in Virtue.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are perfect in virtue, perfect in concentration, perfect in wisdom, and perfect in liberation..."
"Endowed with the knowledge and vision of liberation, they are instructors, informers, revealers, inciters, arouses, and gladdeners;
they are capable of proclaiming the true Dhamma. Monks, I say that even the sight of those monks is of great benefit;
monks, I say that even the hearing of those monks is of great benefit."
“I say, bhikkhus, that approaching those bhikkhus is of great benefit;
I say, bhikkhus, that attending upon those bhikkhus is of great benefit;
I say, bhikkhus, that recollecting those bhikkhus is of great benefit.”
“Monks, I say that even not going forth after those monks is of great benefit.
Why is that? Because, monks, for one who associates with, frequents, and attends upon such monks, even the aggregate of virtuous behavior (sīlakkhandha) may remain incomplete.”
It reaches the fulfillment of its development; even if incomplete, the aggregate of concentration reaches the fulfillment of its development;
even if incomplete, the aggregate of wisdom reaches the fulfillment of its development; even if incomplete, the aggregate of liberation reaches the fulfillment of its development;
even if incomplete, the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation reaches the fulfillment of its development.

And such monks as these, bhikkhus, are called "Teachers," they are called "Caravan Leaders," they are called "Leavers of Strife," they are called "Dispellers of Darkness," they are called "Makers of Light," they are called "Makers of Radiance," they are called "Makers of Lamps," they are called "Bearers of Torches," and they are called "Makers of Splendor."
“They are called ‘noble ones’ (ariya), and they are also called ‘those possessed of vision’ (cakkhumant).
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“This is a ground for joy for those who understand:
namely, those whose selves are cultivated.”
Of the noble ones who live by the Dhamma.
They illuminate the True Dhamma,
they speak as light-makers.
The wise, who create light,
possess vision, and have abandoned conflict—
having heard their teaching, indeed, [one attains peace].
The wise, through right knowledge,
having directly realized the destruction of birth,
do not come to further existence.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fifth.
